newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania shilling stable vs dlr, up on pound.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania shilling stable vs dlr, up on pound.

text.p: The Tanzanian shilling was unchanged against the dollar on Friday, bottoming out after more than two months of slight declines, dealers said.
The shilling exchanged at a commercial mean rate of 600.1380 unchanged from Thursday. Last Friday, it stood at 600.1974.
Against the pound, the shilling stood at a mean rate of 956.1114 from 959.7722 on Thursday. Last Friday, it traded at 968.9717 against the pound.
Financial analysts and dealers said they expected the shilling to remain stable against the dollar and then, appreciate.
"It is stable. Donor funds are coming in on the supply side while there is no new element of demand. We're back to stable demand for imports," said one analyst.
Dealers said the market was quiet, and the business community planned no major moves before the June budget.
"The outlook is one of continued modest upturn. There's expectations about the budget so the business sector has adopted a wait-and-see (attitude)," a dealer said.
But one analyst was eyeing what effects a prolonged drought would have on the economy. The drought could spur a rash of food imports, the analyst said.
"The government may be forced to call on the Bank of Tanzania (BoT) for foreign currency to finance imports of food," said the analyst.
Tanzania, like Kenya, is in the midst of a severe drought and faces the prospect of widespread crop failure.
